newsitem.title: CHINA: Japan loan group arrives in China for talks.
newsitem.headline: Japan loan group arrives in China for talks.

text.p: Japanese officials arrived in Beijing on Wednesday for long-delayed talks on the details of Tokyo's state loans to China, diplomats and officials said.

The loan mission would not discuss the resumption of a Japanese grant-in-aid package worth $63 million that was frozen by Tokyo last year in protest at Beijing's nuclear testing programme, a diplomat in the Chinese capital said.

The $5.3 billion worth of Japanese soft loans due to be extended to China between 1996-1999 were not formally affected by the protest, but Japanese sources in Beijing say settlement of the details of this year's loans is long overdue.
No missions to approve projects for the yen loan package have been sent since China conducted a nuclear test in May.
"This visit has been delayed a long time," said one Japanese source. "They will discuss the volume and details of the loans."

Relations between Beijing and Tokyo have been strained this year by a controversial visit by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to a shrine to Japan's war dead and by a territorial dispute over an island group in the East China Sea.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai on Tuesday warned Japan not to use financial assistance as a form of political pressure.
"Economic cooperation between Japan and China should be established on the basis of equality and mutual benefits," Cui told a news briefing in Beijing.
"To use economic cooperation to apply political pressure is short-sighted and unacceptable and can only affect relations in a negative way," he said.
